title: Table-Recomputation Security with t + 1 Shares
summary: The proof needs twice t plus one shares, while security with t plus one shares in the restricted fixed-probe model remains heuristic and must be proved or refuted by an attack.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the table-recomputation countermeasure is secure with $n = t + 1$ shares in the restricted fixed-probe model. Its formal security proof requires $n \geq 2t + 1$ shares, while security with $n \geq t + 1$ shares in this restricted model is only presented as a heuristic possibility; the unresolved task is to prove security under the lower share bound or exhibit an attack showing that the countermeasure is insecure there.

scope.domain: Side-channel security of a table-recomputation masking countermeasure in the restricted fixed-probe model.
assumptions: Security is considered in the restricted fixed-probe model.
parameters: t: parameter determining the candidate and proof-supported share bounds
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the countermeasure is secure with n = t + 1 shares by proving security under the lower share bound or exhibiting an attack.

citations.label: Higher Order Masking of Look-Up Tables

progress.summary: The paper's formal security proof requires at least 2t + 1 shares, but it remarks that at least t + 1 shares seem heuristically sufficient in the restricted model. The lower-share claim remains unproved, with no attack established.
citation_labels: Jean-Sébastien Coron et al., Higher Order Masking of Look-Up Tables
